decisionMemo.businessProblem: A leveraged regional department-store retailer (30 stores, $600M revenue) is in multi-year decline and must, within roughly 90-120 days, make capital-allocation decisions tied to a refinancing and the next season's merchandise buy. Revenue has fallen from $675M (FY2023) to $642M (FY2024) to $600M (FY2025, -6.5% YoY). Comparable-store sales fell 7%, driven by a 9% drop in store traffic while conversion held roughly flat and average ticket rose 1% — indicating the decline is a traffic/relevance problem, not a conversion or in-store-execution problem. E-commerce grew to 18% of sales ($108M, up from 12%), yet total revenue still declined, so the online channel is not offsetting store losses and appears to reflect cannibalization and share loss rather than additive growth. Gross margin compressed from 38% to 34%, driven primarily by escalating markdowns and inventory write-downs that rose from $9M (1.4% of revenue) to $24M (4.0%), as the company marks down merchandise its customers increasingly do not want. EBITDA fell from $45M (7.0% margin) to $24M (4.0% margin), and about 6 of 30 stores are now EBITDA-negative on a four-wall basis while occupancy cost rises as a share of declining sales. The core challenge: Is the decline driven by a merchandise/demand-planning failure (over-buying causing write-downs), by a cost-structure/unit-economics problem (occupancy and four-wall losses), or by something more fundamental — a structural loss of the banner's relevance and differentiation that is pushing customers to other formats and online? Management must diagnose the true driver before committing the merchandise buy and the refinancing case, because another markdown season could breach covenants.

scenarios.name: Aggressive Recovery (Best Case)

assumptions: Team capacity fully available (no other initiatives)
Client budget approved for all recommended interventions
No external market shocks during implementation
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Revenue recovery within 90 days, competitive positioning restored
risks: Cascading failures if one intervention stumbles

scenarios.name: Staged Implementation (Recommended)

Team capacity for 1-2 major initiatives at a time
Monthly review gates to assess progress and adjust
